      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:07:44 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin to announce presidential bid</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261120-former-french-prime-minister-dominique-de-villepin-to-announce-presidential-bid</link><description>
France’s former conservative prime minister Dominique de Villepin, who served as former president Jacques Chirac’s foreign minister during the country’s steadfast opposition to the US-led invasion of Iraq in 2003, is expected to formally launch his presidential campaign Friday. But while De Villepin’s opposition to Israel’s Gaza campaign and assured analysis of international affairs has caught the eyes of younger voters, it remains to be seen if he can persuade them to cast a ballot for him.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/cd8eccf0-e4c2-11f1-ace1-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B2NA4BB.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/cd8eccf0-e4c2-11f1-ace1-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B2NA4BB.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6df879d0-e4c2-11f1-8e36-0da0c7f0d035</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:31:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/cd8eccf0-e4c2-11f1-ace1-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B2NA4BB.jpg">© Romeo Boetzle, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Middle East</category><title>Iraqi security forces deploy in Hezbollah stronghold under compromise deal</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261120-iraqi-security-forces-to-deploy-in-hezbollah-stronghold-under-compromise-deal</link><description>
Iraqi security forces deployed ​in the Kataib Hezbollah stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhar, state media said on Friday, under a compromise deal brokered by Shi'ite politicians. <![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Thu, 19 Nov 2026 23:42:03 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone ]]> PASADENA, Calif. – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a big milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth, something no other spacecraft has ever done. The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary.

Voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2, flew past Neptune. The gathering served to celebrate Voyager 1's distance milestone: At 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 18), the probe reached one light-day from Earth — the distance a photon travels in one day, which is about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). That means it now takes a full day for a signal to travel from Earth to Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object out in space.

"I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day. What an incredible milestone," Voyager project scientist Linda Spilker said during Thursday's event.

An unexpected, but manageable, anomaly

While this day and this week have been chock-full of excitement over the distance milestone, the Voyager mission team has been hard at work, as usual, keeping the two nearly 50-year-old spacecraft alive and functioning.

Unfortunately, as JPL spokesperson Raquel Villanueva shared at this celebration, on Saturday (Nov. 14), Voyager 1 stopped transmitting science and engineering data. The team has remained in contact with Voyager 1 while investigating the issue, and they are confident that they'll be able to solve it soon.

"We listen to each spacecraft every day," Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd told Space.com at the event. Regarding Voyager 1, "we have an anomaly that is not something unseen before," Dodd said. "We do have a very strong carrier signal. We currently don't have a frame sync, so we're not getting the science or engineering data currently."

"But if you recall," Dodd added, "one light-day is very far from us. [It takes] 24 hours to get the signal to the spacecraft, 24 hours for the signal to come down, so it takes two days to diagnose anything on the spacecraft … So we can't do anything fast, and the data rates are very low."

According to Dodd, this anomaly isn't a major cause for long-term concern. Rather, it's likely just part of the natural aging process for spacecraft.

"These spacecraft are old," she said. "All of us old people have our aches and pains, and you know, sometimes it takes longer to stretch out your muscles and remember things, and so we are in a realm where we're going to see more anomalies with Voyager just due to the distance and the age."

"But we feel Voyager 1, although it's not sending us the telemetry data, it's pointed at the Earth. It's sending us a strong carrier signal, and I'm confident that it won't be too long, and it will send us data back."

And, for anyone curious how Voyager 1's slower twin Voyager 2 is faring, Dodd shared that it is doing very well on its own journey through interstellar space. "Voyager 2 is very healthy. It's continuing its mission. It has three scientific instruments on it," she told Space.com.

"Each spacecraft is basically setting a record every day for longevity or distance," Dodd added about the twin probes.

A heartfelt celebration

Despite the communications anomaly — and even though most of the team had been up all night to confirm the one-light-day signal from Voyager 1 — the room was alive with excitement. The Voyagers have been flying for nearly 50 years on a mission expected to last just five years, so the team was beyond ready to celebrate.

Amidst the more technical updates about the mission and its current status out in interstellar space, the event included footage of Voyager light-day celebrations from around the world. From children cheering on Voyager to iconic landmarks lighting up gold in honor of the mission's Golden Record, the Voyager love echoed around the world in photos and videos. The footage of this international celebration was enough to move Nicky Fox, NASA's associate administrator for the Science Mission Directorate, nearly to tears.

"I actually thought I was going to start sobbing," Fox joked to Space.com after the media briefing. "I think just hearing children's voices and people saying 'We love you, Voyager,' 'Go Voyager' — it just was amazing."

And Fox and the mission team members weren't the only ones sharing their love for Voyager. NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins beamed down her own video message to the Voyager 1 spacecraft from the International Space Station, sharing in the celebration.

"Dear Voyager 1," Watkins said. "As an orbiting outpost just 250 miles [400 kilometers] above Earth, we often feel distant yet deeply connected to our home planet. The International Space Station has had crew continuously living off of the Earth for 26 years, seen hundreds of visitors from around the world, and enabled thousands of experiments to advance space exploration.

"While you have been traveling into the unknown for nearly half a century, helping pave our path, together, our two journeys tell a single story of exploration," she continued. "One remains close to home, and the other reaches ever outward. Voyager 1, you have been a beacon of light, a symbol of exploration, a seeker of truth, a carrier of hope, a brave explorer, traveling further than any human hand has ever reached. You represent the very best of what humanity has to offer.

"As you reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, the entire crew of Expedition 75 and people across the planet send you our admiration and our wishes for a safe and continued journey as you begin your post-one-light-day era. There are so many amazing milestones and discoveries to come. You have a universe ahead of you, and you carry with you our collective hopes and dreams. When we look up from Earth, we will always think of you as you continue forward into the great unknown. May you continue shining bright for all of us. Go Voyager 1!" Watkins said, ending her message with a weightless backflip from aboard the station.

In concluding the media briefing, the mission team invited those in the room who, over the past 50 years (or more, with one person sharing their excitement having worked on Voyager before it was even called Voyager) have worked on the mission in one way or another, to stand up to a round of applause. With mission team members today ranging from those in their 20s to their 90s, the people behind this enduring mission span many generations.

A golden moment

Interestingly, Fox actually began her light-day celebrations earlier in the week. She, alongside writer/producer Ann Druyan — who was the wife of the late astronomer Carl Sagan, whose work helped create the mission's Golden Record and who took the now-famous "pale blue dot" Voyager image of Earth to the public — together lit up the Empire State Building gold.

"I was actually very privileged to flick the switch and turn on the Empire State Building lights on Tuesday evening [Nov. 17]," Fox, wearing golden Voyager-inspired nail polish crafted by her daughter, told Space.com. "That was just spectacular … I was there with Ann … we were both so giddy with the excitement of doing it … It was amazing. And then going up and standing underneath and seeing the tower was just really, really special."

Looking to the future

While the room lit up with excitement for Voyager's light-day milestone on Thursday, the team was also brimming with anticipation for what lies ahead. As Voyager hurtles toward another major milestone, turning 50 in 2027, it remains an active science mission, and the team remains hard at work to push the boundaries of exploration with these aging probes.

"Voyager right now — the two Voyagers — they're in an area of space that we've never been into. So every single bit of data that comes back is precious because it's unique," Fox said.

"Now we're in a region where the sun's influence is a lot different, and we're in this region where we can start to understand: What is it like out past our sun? What is it like in the space between the stars?" Voyager deputy project scientist Jamie Rankin told Space.com. "We're at a very exciting time of starting to connect what we know and what we've seen, living with this star [our sun] to what is out there."

"What's next? Voyager is just going to keep on going. You know, people sometimes think, 'When's the mission going to end?' It's never going to end," Fox added to Space.com. "Even when we can no longer talk to Voyager, they're both going to keep going … So there's no end for the Voyager mission."

On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Hayabusa was supposed to return asteroid samples to Earth.

Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system. We study asteroids to learn more about the solar system's history. Hayabusa (pronounced HI-uh-BOOS-uh) made two touchdowns on asteroid Itokawa (EE -toh-KA-wah). Each time, the spacecraft went into safe mode. Controllers weren't sure if Hayabusa gathered any material. But they sent the spacecraft back to Earth anyway.

Hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010. Scientists found dust of Itokawa inside the capsule, proving that it did indeed capture samples of Itokawa.

Why it mattered

The primary goal of Japan's Hayabusa mission to asteroid Itokawa was never to be the first spacecraft to liftoff from a space rock. The mission was always aimed at collecting samples from an asteroid and returning them to Earth.

It was a hard road to Itokawa for Hayabusa. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) launched the probe on May 9, 2003, with plans for an arrival at the asteroid in the early summer of 2005.

That asteroid arrival was delayed until September 2005 after a solar storm degraded Hayabusa's solar arrays, limiting the available power for its ion engines.

Still, Hayabusa managed to limp along its path to reach the asteroid Itokawa on Sept. 12, 2005.

Hayabusa dropped a small lander onto Itokawa, but that probe was apparently lost. Hayabusa then dropped a landing target on the asteroid, and ultimately managed to touchdown about 99 feet from the marker, JAXA has said.

During its first landing on Nov. 19, Hayabusa descended to a point just 56 feet above Itokawa before going silent for 3 hours, according to an Associated Press report. Once contact was restored, JAXA officials confirmed the probe had landed, and it eventually lifted off for a second attempt. That was the first-ever liftoff from an asteroid by a spacecraft.

"The spacecraft actually bounced off the surface a few times and spent about 39 minutes resting on the asteroid, but apparently the samplers never fired," Andrew Cheng, a Hayabusa science team member at Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, told Space.com at the time. There was hope that some material managed to make it inside the collector anyway.

"After all the thrashing about ... there is no way to confirm that," Cheng had said. The second landing on Itokawa occured a few days later on Nov. 26, 2005.

In November 2010, five months after Hayabusa's sample-return capsule touched down in Australia, JAXA announced some good news: Hayabusa did collect 1,500 dust grains from asteroid Itokawa, samples that were jammed into the collector by the two landings, despite is collector mechanism not firing.

The ultimate success of Hayabusa spurred the creation of another sample-return mission by Japan: Hayabusa2.

That probe launched in December 2014 and arrived at asteroid Ryugu (REE-ooh-goo) in 2018. It collected its own samples and returned them to Earth in December 2020.

The Hayabusa2 probe is now on an extended mission to the asteroid 2015 BM510, which it will fly by in April 2028. It had planned to land on a strange asteroid 1998 KY26, but suffered engine trouble that made that rendezvous impossible

A new set of slo-mo videos gives us a new perspective on SpaceX's first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage.

The company notched the milestone on Saturday (Nov. 14), when the launch tower at its Starbase site in South Texas caught Starship's Ship spacecraft with its "chopstick" arms.

You've probably seen photos and videos showing the epic snag from afar. But on Tuesday (Nov. 17), SpaceX released up-close views — a series of four slo-mo videos captured by cameras near the top of the 480-foot-tall (146 meters) tower.

"The Starbase tower chopsticks catching their first Starship. This unique architecture was designed for full and rapid reusability, enabling repeat launches and landings from the same pad," SpaceX wrote in a Tuesday X post that shared the videos, a compilation of which you can see embedded above.

Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. Its current "V3" version stands about 408 feet (124 m) tall, and future iterations will be even larger.

As SpaceX noted in Tuesday's post, the megarocket is also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first for an orbital launch system. The company plans to catch both Starship stages — Ship and the Super Heavy booster — at the launch tower, a recovery strategy designed to enable efficient inspection, refurbishment and reflight.

SpaceX planned to carry out such a double catch on this most recent test flight, Starship's 15th to date, which launched on Friday evening (Nov. 13). But Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel warning during its return to Starbase about 6.5 minutes after launch and autonomously diverted to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico.

That wasn't a huge deal for SpaceX, as it had already caught Super Heavy on three previous test flights. Snagging Ship is tougher; the upper stage returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter than the booster does.

SpaceX had not even attempted a Ship catch before Flight 15. But the company managed to pull off the maneuver on its first try.

And Ship did some work in orbit before coming home: It deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites on Flight 15, the second batch that the company has sent to low Earth orbit. The first set was deployed on Flight 14, which launched on Sept. 28.

]]> <![CDATA[ China rolls out rocket for launch of 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station (video) ]]>

China's space station is set to receive its first foreign astronaut.

A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov. 17), with launch expected in the next week.

The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV).

China's human spaceflight agency, CMSA, stated that all facilities and equipment at the launch site are in good condition, adding that the launch is scheduled to take place in the coming days, without providing a date.

CMSA typically holds a press conference at Jiuquan a day ahead of launch, during which the crew for the mission is revealed to the public. This time, one of the three crew members will, for the first time, be an international astronaut. One of two Pakistani astronaut candidates will fly to the Tiangong space station on Shenzhou-24, marking a first both for China's outpost and for Pakistan, which will see one its astronauts reach orbit for the first time.

Though public details are sparse, it is thought that the Pakistani astronaut, operating as a payload specialist, will stay aboard Tiangong for around a week, returning home on the departing Shenzhou-23 spacecraft.

One of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts — who are approaching the end of their six-month-long mission, having launched on May 24 — will stay aboard Tiangong for another half a year. This will provide the international visitor with a seat home on Shenzhou-23, and allow a Chinese astronaut to make the country's first year-long stay in orbit. This extra-long mission will supply China with data on physiology ahead of crewed lunar flights and other long-duration missions.

China approved its human spaceflight program in 1992 and launched its first orbital crewed mission in 2003, with Yang Liwei becoming the first Chinese national in space. The country then completed the three-module Tiangong space station in late 2022 and has kept the orbital outpost constantly crewed ever since, with rotating six-month-long missions with brief handovers between crews.

Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed mission and will mark the first time a foreign national is flying on a Shenzhou spacecraft. China is also looking to double the size of Tiangong in the coming years, potentially opening the way to further international missions and space tourist visits.

]]> <![CDATA[ Empire State Building glows gold for NASA's Voyager spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 19, 2026 ]]>

The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov. 17) to celebrate NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hitting one light-day from Earth. And it isn't the only building celebrating this achievement with a sparkling display.

What is it?

Today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth. About 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) away, this is the point at which it takes a full day (or 24 hours) for one light particle to get from us to the probe. So any signal we send to Voyager 1 or it sends back now takes a full day as the spacecraft continues to explore interstellar space.

To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in New York City lit up in gold. This golden glow references the Golden Record onboard both the Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft.

And the Empire State Building wasn't the only major landmark to celebrate the occasion. The Space Needle in Seattle, Washington, and both the Willis Tower and the Skydeck Chicago in Chicago, Illinois have all been illuminated gold to mark the milestone.

Why is it incredible?

The Golden Record that these gold glowing buildings are referencing serves as an inanimate ambassador for Earth, carrying information about humanity, our planet, the other species who live here, the languages we speak, the music we listen to and so much more. It even includes instructions for building a record player to play the record.

The Voyager mission has, and continues to, make incredible scientific discoveries and observations throughout our solar system and now in interstellar space. But this Golden Record provides an additional aspect to the mission that connects us here on Earth to whatever unknown life may exist out there.

If some sort of life forms out in the cosmos were to ever come across Voyager and its Golden Record at any point in the distant future, they might learn a little bit about our small blue dot.

]]> <![CDATA[ Leonid meteor shower thrills stargazers worldwide with colorful sky show (photos/video) ]]> The Leonid meteor shower put on quite the show this week, with bright, colorful meteors thrilling stargazers worldwide and we've got the photos to prove it.

The annual meteor shower peaked overnight on Nov. 17-18, with photographers braving chilly temperatures, clouds and even fog in hopes of catching the perfect shot. And for some, their patience certainly paid off.

Leonids occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. As tiny pieces of comet debris enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of up to 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up, producing bright streaks of light.

The meteor shower is also famous for producing some of the most spectacular meteor storms in history. In fact, this year marks the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, when observers reported an astonishing 40 meteors per second at the peak. To mark the occasion, we spoke to people who witnessed the extraordinary event first-hand and you can read their remarkable accounts in our special feature.

But back to the present! Let's take a look at some of the best photographs and videos captured during this year's impressive display.

Photographer Austin Rebello drove several hours to Nubble Lighthouse in York, Maine, to meet up with fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright and hopefully capture a Leonid or two.

"I specifically drove a few hours up there for hopes of capturing exactly this, as the radiant of the Leonids rose behind the lighthouse," Rebello told Space.com in an email.

"My friend and I were lucky enough to also see it with our eyes, and it was definitely a top 3 meteor for me, as it was even bright enough to briefly cast shadows."

Rebello also revealed on X that the meteor left behind a vibrant blue trail that remained visible to the naked eye for more than 30 seconds.

Fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright was also at Nubble Lighthouse that night, where he captured the lingering trail of a particularly bright meteor on camera for an incredible 12 minutes, according to a post on X.

"Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there," Wright wrote on X.

This phenomenon is known as a persistent meteor train and is created when a bright meteor leaves behind a trail of ionized gas that continues to glow long after the meteor itself has disappeared. These ghostly trails usually fade relatively quickly, but some, like this one, can persist for several minutes. They can twist and change shape as they're carried along by winds high in Earth's atmosphere, according to the BBC Sky at Night Magazine.

Meanwhile, over Deming, New Mexico, photographer Greg Gage had to contend with rather less favorable conditions as clouds and unexpected fog rolled in during the meteor shower's peak.

"While it was perfectly clear when I set up the camera, the night turned out to be mostly cloudy with some light fog," Gage told Space.com in an email.

"But it was just a thin veil and made for some interesting effects. I did catch one meteor through the fog."

But the fog wasn't the only surprise Gage encountered. He also managed to capture a particularly colorful meteor as it blazed through the sky.

"One meteor was rather dramatic. It went through multiple colors as it traveled through the atmosphere," Gage continued.

Gage captured the photographs with a Nikon D5500 and a 14mm lens.

And the colorful displays weren't limited to North America.

In Japan, astronomer Daichi Fujii, curator of the Hiratsuka City Museum, captured a spectacular Leonid fireball streaking across the sky above Hiratsuka in the early hours of Nov. 19.

The brilliant fireball left behind a glowing trail that changed from green to orange as it lingered in the sky.

A fireball is defined as an unusually bright meteor that reaches a visual magnitude of -3 or brighter, according to NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies.

Elsewhere in Japan, skywatcher @simao had a particularly productive night, capturing an impressive 92 meteors between 10:17 p.m. local time on Nov. 18 and 5:40 a.m. on Nov. 19, from central Saitama Prefecture.

But that wasn't all simao captured that night! At 2:19 a.m. on Nov. 19, they caught both a Leonid meteor and a sprite at the same time, looking northwest.

Sprites are very difficult to capture, as they appear as fleeting flashes of light high above thunderstorms, typically appearing as red, jellyfish-like structures.

The Leonids were already making an appearance in the days leading up to the shower's peak.

On Nov. 16, astrophotographer @EricTheSpaceCat captured several possible Leonids streaking through the sky.

If the Leonids have left you wanting more, you won't have to wait long for another significant meteor shower! Next up are the Geminids, one of the most prolific meteor showers of the year, which will peak overnight on Dec. 13-14. And 2026 is shaping up to be a particularly good year for them. With only a slender waxing crescent moon in the sky, moonlight interference will be minimal, giving skywatchers a chance to spot up to 120 Geminid meteors per hour under ideal conditions.

For the best views, head somewhere dark, away from city lights, and give your eyes around 30 minutes to adjust to the darkness.

   <description>Škrtila koťata a vší silou s nimi házela o silnici, uškrtila i dva psy, ač ji měli rádi. Zapálila kůlnu a dva stohy. Nenáviděla lidi a strašně moc chtěla zabíjet.       <title>Do Polska dopadl neznámý objekt. Střela Ch-101 nebo dron, míní armáda</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/ruske-utoky-vyvolaly-poplach-v-polsku.A261120_073601_zahranicni_ijan#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Vzdušný prostor nad jihovýchodem Polska byl v noci narušen. Úřady v Lublinském vojvodství dopoledne potvrdily, že v okrese Bilgoraj byl nalezen dosud neidentifikovaný objekt. Mluvčí armády uvedl, že může jít o střelu Ch-101 nebo proudový dron. Polský premiér Donald Tusk ujistil, že v Polsku aktuálně nehrozí nebezpečí vzdušného útoku.  <description>Ukrajinské drony v noci na pátek zaútočily na chemický závod u města Dorogobuž v ruské Smolenské oblasti, který vyrábí mimo jiné složky do výbušnin.  <description>Ve čtvrtek se v Berlíně sešla takzvaná koalice ochotných, ta se zaměřuje na podporu Ukrajiny. Německý kancléř Friedrich Merz na závěrečné tiskovce prohlásil, že Koalice dospěla k širokému konsenzu, pokud jde o finanční pomoc pro Ukrajinu. O tom, co si reálně od jednání můžeme slibovat hovoří pro Radiožurnál David Mareček, odborník na transatlantické vztahy z Katedry mezinárodních vztahů a evropských studií Pražské metropolitní univerzity.</description>

 <description>Koalice ochotných bude i v celém příštím roce Ukrajinu podporovat. Po jednání více než čtyř desítek členů koalice v Berlíně to řekl německý kancléř Friedrich Merz. Ruského prezidenta Vladimira Putina vyzval, aby válku proti Ukrajině ukončil a začal jednat o míru. Ukrajina musí podle Merze dostat silné bezpečnostní garance a koalice ochotných je připravena přispět k zajištění budoucího míru.</description>

 <description>Mezinárodní soudní dvůr (ICJ) ve čtvrtek rozhodl, že tisíce vražd a rozsáhlé sexuální násilí, kterých se v roce 2017 dopustily bezpečnostní složky v Barmě na příslušnících skupiny Rohingů, představují genocidu podporovanou státem. Soudní dvůr uvedl, že záměrem Barmy tehdy bylo zničit významnou část příslušníků této muslimské menšiny. Je to poprvé, kdy nejvyšší soud OSN shledal nějaký stát odpovědným za genocidu.</description>

 <description>Ministr životního prostředí Igor Červený (Motoristé sobě) se vypravil na svou první klimatickou konferenci OSN v Turecku. V národním projevu označil za českou prioritu adaptaci na změnu klimatu a mluvil o rizicích dekarbonizace. V rozhovoru pro iROZHLAS.cz označuje snahu o odklon od fosilních paliv za náboženství a uklidňuje tichomořské národy ohrožené stoupáním oceánů. Slibuje také projednání petice k odvolání šéfa Krkonošského národního parku.</description>

S tím ale přijde ochlazení a v pondělí pak také sněžení, a to v nižších polohách. Chladnější počasí pak vydrží i v dalších dnech.</description></item><item><title>Do porodnice to nestihli. Jakub se narodil v sanitce kousek od Mníšku</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/906221-do-porodnice-to-nestihli-jakub-se-narodil-v-sanitce-kousek-od-mnisku.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/906221-do-porodnice-to-nestihli-jakub-se-narodil-v-sanitce-kousek-od-mnisku.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 06:04:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Už ve třicátém týdnu se ve čtvrtek narodil malý Jakub. To je předčasné, ale stále to není až tak výjimečné. Jenže miminko se nenarodilo v porodnici, kam mířilo, ale v sanitce nedaleko Liberce.</description></item><item><title>Silničáři v Libereckém kraji zavřou v noci na sobotu silnici kolem přehrady Souš</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906209-silnicari-v-libereckem-kraji-zavrou-v-noci-na-sobotu-silnici-kolem-prehrady.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906209-silnicari-v-libereckem-kraji-zavrou-v-noci-na-sobotu-silnici-kolem-prehrady.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 20:01:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Silničáři v Libereckém kraji uzavřou o půlnoci na sobotu pro dopravu silnici druhé třídy 290 kolem přehrady Souš v Jizerských horách. Důvodem je vývoj počasí, řekla mluvčí Libereckého kraje Michaela Křivková.</description></item><item><title>Zlaté detaily a pevný kámen. Libštátský most má zpět své dva patrony</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906070-zlate-detaily-a-pevny-kamen-libstatsky-most-ma-zpet-sve-dva-patrony.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906070-zlate-detaily-a-pevny-kamen-libstatsky-most-ma-zpet-sve-dva-patrony.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 17:55:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Historický kamenný most přes řeku Olešku v Libštátě opět zdobí sochy sv. Jana Nepomuckého a sv. Václava. Liberecký kraj za jejich záchranu zaplatil přibližně 461 tisíc korun. Restaurátor při obnově zastavil drolení pískovce, ošetřil kovové prvky a navrátil památkám zlacené detaily i nápisy.</description></item><item><title>Liberec má nové zastupitelstvo i primátora. Tím se stal Lukáš Hájek</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/906205-liberec-ma-nove-zastupitelstvo-i-primatora-tim-se-stal-lukas-hajek.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/906205-liberec-ma-nove-zastupitelstvo-i-primatora-tim-se-stal-lukas-hajek.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 17:29:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>V Liberci proběhlo ustavující zastupitelstvo. Slib složilo 39 nových zastupitelů, primátorem se stal Lukáš Hájek (Starostové pro LK). Ten nahradil Jaroslava Zámečníka, který byl primátorem posledních osm let. Ve vedení města ale zůstává, bude ekonomickým náměstkem.</description></item><item><title>Nové vedení Liberce podepsalo koaliční smlouvu. Nejprve se podívá na rozpočet</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906195-nove-vedeni-liberce-podepsalo-koalicni-smlouvu-nejprve-se-podiva-na-rozpocet.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906195-nove-vedeni-liberce-podepsalo-koalicni-smlouvu-nejprve-se-podiva-na-rozpocet.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:53:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Nová trojkoalice složená ze Starostů pro Liberecký kraj, Lepšího Liberce a Pirátů s Libercem otevřeným lidem podepsala koaliční smlouvu. Jako první chce řešit rozpočet na příští rok.</description></item><item><title>V centru Jablonce vyroste parkovací dům pro 256 aut</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906143-v-centru-jablonce-vyroste-parkovaci-dum-pro-256-aut.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906143-v-centru-jablonce-vyroste-parkovaci-dum-pro-256-aut.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 12:34:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Radnice v Jablonci připravuje výstavbu nového parkovacího domu. Ten vyroste v ulici 5. května a naváže na vznikající Terminál veřejné osobní dopravy. Nabídne 265 míst i plochy pro obchody. Město předpokládá, že výstavba vyjde na 280 milionů bez daně.</description></item><item><title>Cestujte po Libereckém kraji za polovinu: S kartou ISIC vyřídíte slevu z domova</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/899084-cestujte-po-libereckem-kraji-za-polovinu-s-kartou-isic-vyridite-slevu-z-domova.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/899084-cestujte-po-libereckem-kraji-za-polovinu-s-kartou-isic-vyridite-slevu-z-domova.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:42:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Chystáte se do školy, na kroužky, trénink nebo za zábavou o víkendu? Pokud je vám od 6 do 26 let, v síti Integrované dopravy Libereckého kraje (IDOL) lze cestovat se slevou 50 % z plného jízdného.</description></item><item><title>Cvak, cvak, zapni pás. Písnička učí děti bezpečně cestovat autem</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906044-cvak-cvak-zapni-pas-pisnicka-uci-deti-bezpecne-cestovat-autem.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906044-cvak-cvak-zapni-pas-pisnicka-uci-deti-bezpecne-cestovat-autem.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:53:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Doprava</category><description>Dítě v autosedačce ještě nemusí být v bezpečí. Rozhoduje i správné připoutání, dotažení pásů nebo to, co má na sobě a v rukou. Nová písnička Karol a Kvída Cvak, cvak, zapni pás učí děti jednoduchý návyk: než se auto rozjede, musí být připoutané. Vznikla v rámci kampaně Cestujte s dětmi bezpečně.</description></item><item><title>Tohle je málo, měl by říct Denia. A ne být na hráče po sestupu do béčka Ligy národů hrdý</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906140-tohle-je-malo-mel-by-rict-denia-a-ne-byt-na-hrace-po-sestupu-do-becka-ligy-narodu-hrdy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906140-tohle-je-malo-mel-by-rict-denia-a-ne-byt-na-hrace-po-sestupu-do-becka-ligy-narodu-hrdy.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:54:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Pavel Hartman</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Šest porážek v řadě, děsivé skóre 3:14, jednoznačný sestup z áčka do béčka Ligy národů. Přesto od generálního manažera české reprezentace slyšíme, že musíme pokračovat v téhle cestě, o které ví, že je správná. A hlavní trenér národního mužstva pronese, že je na hráče hrdý.</description></item></channel></rss>

V pondělí 9. 11. 2026 se uskutečnilo ustavující zasedání Zastupitelstva města Jiříkov, které zahájilo nové čtyřleté volební období 2026–2030. Na programu bylo především složení slibu nově zvolených zastupitelů, volba vedení města a dalších orgánů samosprávy.
